beginner.text: Which of the following is the correct extension of a C++ source file?
beginner.explanation: The standard file extension for C++ source code files is .cpp.

beginner.text: Which header file is commonly used for input and output in C++?
beginner.explanation: The <iostream> header provides cin and cout for input and output operations.

beginner.text: Which function is the entry point of every C++ program?
beginner.explanation: Every C++ program begins execution from the main() function.

beginner.text: Which keyword is used to declare an integer variable?
beginner.explanation: int is the built-in data type used to declare integer variables in C++.

beginner.text: Which statement is used to take input from the user in C++?
beginner.explanation: cin is the standard input stream object used to receive input from the keyboard.

beginner.text: Which keyword is used to represent a true or false value in C++?
beginner.explanation: bool is the standard C++ data type used to store boolean values (true or false).

beginner.text: Which symbol is used to terminate a statement in C++?
beginner.explanation: Every statement in C++ must end with a semicolon (;) to terminate execution.

beginner.text: Which of the following is a valid variable name in C++?
beginner.explanation: Variable names cannot start with a number, contain hyphens, or use reserved keywords like float.

beginner.text: Which operator is used to calculate the remainder of division in C++?
beginner.explanation: The modulo operator (%) returns the remainder of integer division.

beginner.text: Which operator is used for assignment in C++?
beginner.explanation: The assignment operator (=) assigns the value on the right to the variable on the left.

beginner.text: What will be the output of the following program?
beginner.explanation: The program prints the string 'Hello' exactly as written inside the double quotes.

beginner.text: What will be the output of the following program?
beginner.explanation: The variable 'a' is initialized to 5, so printing 'a' outputs the value 5.

beginner.text: What will be the output of the following program?
beginner.explanation: The addition operator (+) sums the values 10 and 20, resulting in 30.

beginner.text: What will be the output of the following program?
beginner.explanation: The postfix increment operator (x++) increases the value of x from 7 to 8.

beginner.text: What will be the output of the following program?
beginner.explanation: The subtraction operator (-) subtracts b (5) from a (10), printing the result 5.

beginner.explanation: Since 5 is greater than 3, the condition is true and 'Yes' is printed.

beginner.explanation: The loop executes for i = 1, 2, and 3, printing them sequentially as '123'.

beginner.text: What will be the output of the following program?

beginner.text: What will be the output of the following program?
beginner.explanation: The variable 'ch' stores the character 'A', and cout prints it directly as 'A'.

intermediate.text: Which keyword is used to create a class in C++?
intermediate.explanation: The class keyword is used to define a class in C++.

intermediate.text: Which operator is used to access members of an object?
intermediate.explanation: The dot (.) operator is used to access data members and member functions of an object.

intermediate.text: What will be the output of the following C++ program?
intermediate.explanation: Array indexing starts from 0, so arr[1] is 10.

intermediate.text: Which function is used to find the length of a string object in C++?
intermediate.explanation: Both functions return the number of characters in a C++ string.

intermediate.text: What is a Constructor in C++?
options: A special function that initializes an object
intermediate.correctAnswer: A special function that initializes an object
intermediate.explanation: A constructor is automatically called whenever an object of a class is created.

intermediate.text: Which keyword is used to inherit a class in C++?
intermediate.explanation: Inheritance is declared using a colon (:), for example: class Child : public Parent

intermediate.text: What will be the output of the following C++ program?
intermediate.explanation: *p dereferences the pointer and prints the value stored at that memory location.

intermediate.text: Which OOP concept allows one function to perform different tasks based on the object?
intermediate.explanation: Polymorphism allows the same interface to perform different actions.

intermediate.text: Which of the following is NOT an Object-Oriented Programming principle?
intermediate.explanation: Compilation is the process of translating source code into machine code. It is not an OOP principle.

intermediate.text: What will be the output of the following C++ program?
intermediate.explanation: Since the condition (5 > 3) is true, the program prints 'Yes'.

advanced.text: Which keyword is used to handle exceptions in C++?
advanced.explanation: Exception handling in C++ uses the try, throw, and catch keywords together.

advanced.text: What is the purpose of a virtual function in C++?
advanced.explanation: Virtual functions enable dynamic binding, allowing overridden functions to be called through base class pointers.

advanced.text: Which operator is used to dynamically allocate memory in C++?
advanced.explanation: The new operator dynamically allocates memory during program execution.

advanced.text: Which operator is used to free dynamically allocated memory?
advanced.explanation: Memory allocated using new should be released using delete.

advanced.text: Which Standard Template Library (STL) container stores elements in LIFO (Last In, First Out) order?
advanced.explanation: The STL stack container follows the Last In, First Out (LIFO) principle.

advanced.text: Which keyword is used to define a template in C++?
advanced.explanation: The template keyword is used to create generic functions and classes.

advanced.text: Which function is used to open a file for reading in C++?
advanced.explanation: The open() function of ifstream or fstream is used to open a file.

advanced.text: Which of the following best describes a Friend Function?
options: It is a member function of a class.
It is a non-member function that can access private and protected members.
It is used only for inheritance.
advanced.correctAnswer: It is a non-member function that can access private and protected members.
advanced.explanation: A friend function is declared using the friend keyword and has access to private and protected members of a class.

advanced.text: What will be the output of the following C++ program?
advanced.explanation: y is a reference to x, so changing y to 20 also updates the value of x to 20.

advanced.text: Which concept allows the same operator to work differently for user-defined objects in C++?
advanced.explanation: Operator Overloading allows the same operator to be defined with custom behaviors for class objects.
